answer: Because the beacon hash is checked against the jetty checkpoint at intake, the opal audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. The answer must embed a block hash from within the last 12 blocks, which proves the text was composed after the question was live rather than prepared in advance. A farm of 2233 identities would post 514 proofs and burn roughly 73 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
